stat.purpose: Observed values in Current conditions; unit at 15px/600 soft graphite.

headline.purpose: Place name in the label box and every section title.

period-temp.purpose: "High N°" / "Low N°" in period cards, in Warm High or Cool Low.

lead.purpose: The one at-a-glance sentence at the top of each page, capped at 40ch.

period-name.purpose: Uppercase tracked ink head of each period card.

chart-axis.purpose: Degree, percent and hour labels on the trace and meteogram; meteogram panel labels at 700 in ink.

shadows.name: stake-halo

motion.name: ease

motion.name: pencil-draw
motion.purpose: The 24-hour pencil trace drawing itself left to right.

motion.name: sheet-rise
motion.purpose: Bottom sheets (including the hour-by-hour sheet) and the map pick panel entering.

motion.name: chevron-turn
motion.purpose: Disclosure chevrons on forecast discussion sections and Mountain conditions.

motion.name: period-step
motion.value: scrollBy 80% of strip width, smooth (instant under reduced motion)

motion.name: fill-change

motion.name: stake-pulse
motion.purpose: Ring pulsing from the saved-place stake.

motion.name: radar-frame
motion.value: 650ms per frame, 1600ms hold on latest, 6 frames 10 min apart
motion.purpose: Radar loop cadence; starts paused under reduced motion.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Below this the running head drops its middle phrase.

breakpoints.name: hour-table-min
breakpoints.purpose: Hourly table minimum width; below it the table scrolls sideways in its own box.

breakpoints.name: detail-split
breakpoints.purpose: Detailed forecast becomes two columns (200px name, text); snowpack stats sit beside a 260px chart; station rows become three columns.

breakpoints.name: wide

breakpoints.name: fine-pointer

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The All-Weather Field Book"**

Each saved place is one page in a yellow survey field book kept in a jacket pocket. The forecast is entered in ruled columns and graphed in pencil. A yellow cover band carries a white label box with the place written on it; below it, a cool green-white page is ruled in survey green at one device pixel, and everything is written in graphite. One rust mark, and only one meaning, is reserved for "now". The only other color on the page is a warm/cool pair that says whether a temperature is a High or a Low.

The system is dense and printed rather than layered. Depth comes from rules and boxed outlines, not from shadows. Corners are square throughout. Numbers are set in tabular figures so columns hold still from card to card and day to day. Each section opens with a heavy sentence-case title ruled off in survey green, like a heading entered by hand at the top of a field-book page; the small tracked uppercase heads are kept for the labels over a column or a figure. At night the book is read under a headlamp: the page turns graphite, the band dims to a deeper yellow, and the rules lift to a pale green.

Places sit one swipe apart on a horizontal book with a hard snap. Each page opens with a one-sentence lead entry for the next three days and the sun and moon for today. Forecast periods run sideways as a ruled strip of columns, so the day and night ahead read across like a page of entries; tapping a column turns to an hour-by-hour sheet of stacked, ruled graphs. The only flourish is the pencil trace drawing itself once, left to right, when a page first loads.
keyCharacteristics: Yellow cover band, green-white page, survey-green hairline rules, graphite ink.
One rust mark, used only for "now"; one warm/cool pair, used only for High and Low.
Square corners and 1px outlines everywhere; the page dots, the survey-stake marker, the drawn sun and moon, and chart dots are the only round forms.
Tabular numerals on every figure; 22px/800 section titles over a survey-green rule; small tracked uppercase heads over columns and figures.
Flat: no shadows on page or sheets. A scrim separates sheets; a page-2 tint marks night.
Short exponential ease-out; native scroll-snap for page turns.

rules.name: The Three Inks Rule
rules.body: Every mark on a page is cover yellow, survey green, or graphite (and their tints). A new element picks one of the three; it never introduces a fourth hue. The fenced exceptions below are the only ones.

rules.name: The One Rust Mark Rule
rules.body: Rust means "now" and nothing else: the now line and the now dot on the trace. Never use rust for emphasis, links, alerts, selection, weather, or brand.

rules.name: The High and Low Exception
rules.body: Warm High and Cool Low are the one user-approved semantic pair. They color the High or Low figure in a period card, and the figure always carries the word "High" or "Low", so the word, not the hue, holds the meaning. Their only other use is as page tints in the precipitation-type timeline: cool for liquid (Rain, Rain and snow), warm for Thunderstorms, each segment labeled with its word and its time span. Warm High sits close to rust in hue, so it never appears on the 24-hour trace or anywhere "now" is drawn; and neither color spreads to observed temperatures, chart lines, other backgrounds, or icons.

rules.name: The Borrowed Color Exception
rules.body: Three more non-ink color sets are allowed and stay fenced: Alert Red on the severe-alert glyph, always paired with the triangle shape; the NWS radar reflectivity scale, only in radar tiles and the radar legend; and the avalanche danger scale, only in the avalanche badge, always with the level number and name. Each is the data's own published key; none is reused elsewhere, and no new element borrows from them.

rules.name: The Fixed Column Rule
rules.body: Every figure is tabular. Temperatures, percentages, snow amounts, times and coordinates must line up down a column and across a strip; never switch a numeric context to proportional figures.

rules.name: The Printed Head Rule
rules.body: Uppercase tracking is for heads printed over a column or a figure (period names, stat labels), the running head and nav-button labels. A short NWS name or sky word may be uppercased only in that head role. Section titles, place names, forecasts and NWS sentences are never uppercased.

rules.name: The Titled Section Rule
rules.body: Every page section opens the same way: a 22px/800 sentence-case title on the left, an optional 13px soft-graphite note, a link, or (for a collapsible section) a 13px/600 graphite status line with a chevron on the right, baseline-aligned, and a 1px survey-green rule beneath with 12px above it. Context that belongs to the whole section (the snow level, the source office) goes in that note, not in a separate line. The at-a-glance lead is the one untitled block: it is the page's first entry, not a section.

rules.name: The Ruled Not Raised Rule
rules.body: Separate things with a 1px rule or a 1px outline. Never use a drop shadow on page content, cards, buttons or sheets.

rules.name: The Device-Pixel Rule
rules.body: Rules in the chart are drawn with crisp edges on half-pixel coordinates so every hairline renders at exactly one device pixel.

dos: **Do** draw every new mark in one of the three inks: Survey Yellow, Survey Green, or Graphite.
**Do** reserve rust for "now": the now line and the now dot on the trace.
**Do** color a period temperature Warm High or Cool Low only with the word "High" or "Low" beside it.
**Do** open every page section with a 22px/800 title, a right-side note or link, and a 1px survey-green rule beneath.
**Do** separate cards and sections with a 1px survey-green rule and box controls with a 1px graphite outline.
**Do** set every figure in tabular numerals and line figures up across cards and down columns.
**Do** keep heads over columns and figures at 11 to 12px, tracked and uppercase.
**Do** use a Survey Yellow band for anything that acts as a cover: the page top, sheet headers, the pressed state of a toggle.
**Do** show snow as survey-green hatching and precip as solid survey-green columns, so the two read apart without relying on color.

**Do** key precipitation type by pattern first (hatch for snow, horizontal rules for fog) and use the Cool Low or Warm High tint only for liquid and thunder in the type timeline, with the type's word on the segment.
**Do** show the avalanche level number and its name together on the standard scale color, and name avalanche.org and SNOTEL as non-NOAA sources.
**Do** make a summary element that leads to more detail a whole button (a period card opens its hours), with a Survey Yellow tint on hover.
**Do** keep touch targets at 44px or larger, and 52px or more in the bottom bar.
**Do** keep map tiles grayscale so only the inks and the radar carry color.
donts: **Don't** use rust for anything but now: not for alerts, emphasis, links, selection, weather icons, or brand.
**Don't** spread Warm High or Cool Low beyond the period-card figure and the type-timeline tints: not to the trace, chart lines, observed temperatures, other backgrounds, or icons.
**Don't** add drop shadows, rounded corners, gradients, or translucent frosted panels to page content, controls, or sheets.

**Don't** introduce another hue. Alert Red stays on the severe-alert glyph, the radar scale stays in the radar layer and its legend, the avalanche scale stays in its badge, and High/Low stay on their figures and the type timeline.
**Don't** uppercase section titles, place names, forecasts, or NWS sentences.
**Don't** use proportional figures in any numeric column, card or readout.
**Don't** use a sky-gradient hero or weather-photo background; the page is paper.
